prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” roofing company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and timeline. Instead of naming one company (which I can do if you give your ZIP code), here’s a practical guide so you can identify the best hurricane‑rated roof contractor in Miami and avoid scams.

What the best contractors have
- Florida roofing license (verify at the FL DBPR license lookup).  
- Full general liability and workers’ comp insurance.  
- Experience with Miami‑Dade County building code and Miami‑Dade County NOA (Notice of Acceptance) products and installation methods.  
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.).  
- Written, multi‑year workmanship warranty plus manufacturer material warranty.  
- Good local references and strong recent reviews (Google/Yelp/BBB).  
- Will pull permits and provide inspection records.

What to ask every contractor
1. Are you licensed in Florida and insured? Can you provide license and insurance numbers?  
2. Do you use products with Miami‑Dade NOAs? Provide NOA numbers for the materials and installation details.  
3. Do you have manufacturer certification (give proof)?  
4. Will you pull permits and schedule inspections? (Don’t accept “no permits” or cash deals.)  
5. What is included in the written estimate and warranty (labor, materials, tear‑off, disposal)?  
6. Can you provide recent local references and photos of completed hurricane‑rated roofs?  
7. How do you handle storm‑related insurance claims and mitigation credits?

Red flags
- No license or insurance, or refusal to provide numbers.  
- Door‑to‑door offers right after a storm (storm chasers).  
- Pressure to sign immediately or heavy upfront cash requests.  
- No permit pull or refusal to use NOA‑approved materials.  
- Very low bids that sound too good to be true.

How to vet companies quickly
- Check FL DBPR license lookup (verify contractor name and license status).  
- Check Miami‑Dade Product Control NOA list for the materials they propose.  
- Read recent online reviews and complaint history (BBB).  
- Ask your insurance agent for recommended or approved contractors.  
- Get at least 3 written bids with the same scope for apples‑to‑apples comparison.

If you want, I can:
- Find top‑rated hurricane‑rated roofing contractors near you (tell me your Miami ZIP code or neighborhood), or  
- Draft a short email or checklist you can send to contractors to compare bids.

Which would you prefer?
